scope: Shared frontend preview runtime and deferred PDF initialization; no new conversion algorithms or Go changes.
changes: Replacement/destruction settle superseded preview calls even when a converter or driver ignores cancellation; late success and rejection remain observed and discarded.
Each load owns its signal through background resource work, including after initial load resolves.
Rejected loads detach and destroy their failed session, abort its signal and expose the error in getState and the error event. An unrelated AbortError is reported rather than leaving a spinner.
Driver error events remain visible through initial load completion until an explicit state update recovers.
PDF.js and its worker URL load only when opening a PDF. The demo places the PDF engine in its own dynamic chunk, preserving route-only imports in Node without DOMMatrix.
Detach subscriptions/session before teardown callbacks; token checks preserve previews opened by loading, warning, abort, factory or destroy callbacks, and stop obsolete event delivery.
limits: Already-started synchronous work cannot be interrupted; non-cooperative asynchronous work may finish after the caller stops waiting.
Custom drivers remain responsible for their own DOM and resource cleanup; the runtime cannot prevent arbitrary DOM writes by a non-cooperative custom driver.
The initial load promise does not guarantee every browser image/media resource has finished decoding.

performance.note: Correctness checks only; no load-time, throughput, memory or peer-ranking claim. Existing external benchmark totals remain unchanged.

developmentBrowser.command: npx playwright test apps/demo/e2e/preview-runtime.e2e.ts apps/demo/e2e/pdf-lifecycle.e2e.ts apps/demo/e2e/native-lifecycle.e2e.ts apps/demo/e2e/converter-io.e2e.ts --workers=1

checks: Demo broken DOCX → readable text recovery
Real DOCM conversion with all four decoded pictures
No PDF engine request during text preview; exactly one when PDF opens, complete canvas pixels contain ink, text replacement removes canvases

diagnostics: The initial category-boundary check failed because eager PDF.js evaluated DOMMatrix in Node. Deferred runtime/worker imports fix the real failure; the original failure and final successful category logs are retained.

Initial new test routes used FormatRoute instead of FormatDefinition, leaving converter work unobserved in the test fixture. Corrected before the final old-source regression proof; initial failed log retained.
The first current-source focused run used a matcher unavailable in installed Vitest. Replaced with separate count and argument assertions; failed log retained.
Final unit and browser checks have no unhandled errors. Existing Three.js duplicate-instance and production vendor chunk-size warnings remain.

loadingArtifacts.note: Production entry, module preloads and CSS as reported by the bundle-size script; bytes are compressed artifacts, not measured network transfer or elapsed time. PDF engine is requested exactly once when opening PDF, zero times for preceding text preview.

reproduction: From each listed package directory: ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run
Use an isolated current source copy preserving prior changes, reverse only preview-runtime.patch and run the same 18-test file: 15 fail, 3 controls pass.
